prompt.en: A timer was designed for a pair of equal capacitors in parallel, but they were wired in series. How does the actual total compare with the planned total?

text.en: It is unchanged because the same parts were used.

feedback.en: Connection changes the total even when the parts stay the same.

text.en: It is half the planned total.

feedback.en: The series total is half a single part, but the plan called for twice a single part.

text.en: It is a quarter of the planned total.

feedback.en: For each value C, the plan gives 2 x C and the actual circuit gives C / 2. Their ratio is 1/4.

text.en: It is four times the planned total.

feedback.en: That reverses the comparison. The actual series total is smaller, not larger.

explanation.en: Check both the intended topology and the actual topology before comparing their totals.

prompt.en: A bypass capacitor chosen to shunt unwanted RF is reused against much lower-frequency interference. With its value unchanged, why might it shunt less effectively?

text.en: Its reactance is higher at the lower frequency.

feedback.en: A higher capacitive reactance gives the unwanted current a harder shunt path.

text.en: Its reactance is lower at the lower frequency.

feedback.en: That reverses the capacitor trend and would predict an easier shunt path.

text.en: Its reactance stays unchanged because its capacitance label has not changed.

feedback.en: A fixed capacitance still has frequency-dependent reactance. The label alone does not fix its opposition.

text.en: Only lead length matters, so the capacitor's frequency response can be ignored.

feedback.en: Lead layout can matter, but the capacitor's reactance still changes with frequency and affects the shunt path.

explanation.en: A cure selected for one frequency range may work poorly in another, even with the same connection.

prompt.en: A series tuned circuit is at resonance. Its capacitance is then increased while the source frequency stays fixed. What happens?

text.en: It remains exactly resonant because the resistance stayed the same.

feedback.en: Resistance affects losses and sharpness. L and C set the ideal resonant frequency.

text.en: Its resonant frequency falls, so the source is now above resonance.

feedback.en: More capacitance lowers the resonant frequency; the unchanged source now lies above it.

text.en: Its resonant frequency rises, so the source is now below resonance.

feedback.en: More capacitance lowers, rather than raises, the resonant frequency.

text.en: Its resonant frequency falls, so the unchanged source is now below resonance.

feedback.en: The direction of the frequency shift is right, but the comparison is reversed. The source stayed at the old, higher frequency.

explanation.en: Resonance is a frequency condition as well as a circuit arrangement. Changing C moves that condition.
